findings: def:causally_open_spacetime_open (ETT.tex:694-697) as printed, with J⁺_U(V) open only, is STRICTLY WEAKER than the two-sided reading DEC-8 made the definition of record (registers/DECISIONS.md:19): the gated line (ℝ ⊕ Unit, Hausdorff, second countable; causal, globally hyperbolic, strongly causal, curves extending, locally push-up, two-sided locally causally open) satisfies the printed definition and not the ruled one, because J⁻_M({⋆}) = (−∞, 10] ∪ {⋆} is not open while {⋆} is (Causal.gateLine_separates_causallyOpen). DEC-8's '±' is therefore a change of the notion, not a restatement: a statement of the paper that cites causal openness and uses only J⁺ holds under the printed form; one that uses J⁻ (as prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality (ii)⇒(i) does, ETT.tex:741-748) needs the ruled form. When the definition gains its ± (DEC-8's note), the change is substantive.

The counterexample is not absolutely minimal (non-local), so it says nothing about absolutely minimal spacetimes; it shows that the absolute minimality of prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal (ETT.tex:698-701, DEC-8 reading) cannot be dropped: locally two-sided causally open does not give causally open.

Likewise the causal arc-connectedness of lem:pushup_local (ETT.tex:557-560) cannot be dropped: the gated line has a cover by opens with push-up (the line and {⋆}) and no push-up (Causal.gateLine_separates_pushUp). The paper assumes the hypothesis, so this is a sharpness remark, not a defect.
